description: Hi everyone!  We are Anshika Mathur, Anush Ramakrishna , Dhanush J , Dhruv Gupta , Sathwika Kulkarni and Vidhi, a team participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge. We are passionate about space, technology, creativity, and solving real-world problems. We’re looking for enthusiastic teammates with skills in coding, design, research, or data analysis who love sharing ideas and learning together. Let’s collaborate, innovate, and aim for the stars!
summary:
Mars Atlas is an interactive 3D Martian GIS and Extravehicular Activity (EVA) survival planner built for the Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map challenge. Using CesiumJS configured to the true IAU-2015 Martian ellipsoid (3,396.19 km equatorial radius) and a Python FastAPI scientific backend, it transforms fragmented NASA datasets into a unified mission control console.

Explorers can toggle five orbital layers: Viking true-color imagery, NASA MGS MOLA 32 ppd elevation (1.44 km/px with real 3D mesh terrain), Horn 3×3 slope-hazard maps, pole-to-pole THEMIS Night-IR thermal inertia (distinguishing solid bedrock from dust traps), and Mars Odyssey GRS + TES Dust Cover Index maps across 10 surface elements (H₂O, Fe, Si, S, Cl, K, Th, Al, Ca, DCI). A slope-penalized A* pathfinder routes astronauts and rovers safely around steep crater walls while computing live oxygen, battery, cooling water, radiation, walk-back limits, and Mars Sol Date / Local Mean Solar Time, validated against real Perseverance and Curiosity rover traverses.

By uniting hazard avoidance, resource mapping, and life-support telemetry in one tool, Mars Atlas helps keep future Martian explorers alive.
